manifest.name: dsh-session-requirement
manifest.description: Per-conversation requirement / constraint box for DeepSeek Harness, in the conversation title row behind a GUI switch, with @-skill selection, injected into every request of that conversation.

bundle.text:
# The dsh-session-requirement bundle patch: one host row that owns the
# per-conversation requirement state, the HTTP API used by the browser half,
# and the `agent/pre-step` injection. The `dsh.client` browser bundle ships
# in the same package.
- insert:
    - id: session-requirement
      name: 'dsh-session-requirement'

readme.text:
Per-conversation **session requirement / constraint** box for DeepSeek Harness.
It lives in the conversation title row and lets you write one standing
requirement for *this* conversation, plus pick skills with `@`, and have all of
it attached to every message you send.

The box is **off until you switch it on**. The switch lives in
**Settings → General → 本对话的整体要求**; flip it and the box appears in the
title row immediately — no reload, no restart. Flip it back and the box is gone,
and nothing is attached to your messages either.

Collapsed, it is one line at the right end of the title row:

```
… 标准模式                              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
                                        │ 输入本对话的限制、约束或整体要求（可选）(●)│
                                        └────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Focused, it lifts out of the row as a floating card — the header never grows:

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- || GUI switch | one toggle in Settings → General, stored globally in the state file; off on a fresh install |
| Show/hide | off renders nothing at all — no empty gap and no slot in the title row; on mounts the field in every conversation at once |
| Placement | `conversation.session.header.utilities`, `order: 0` — the right-aligned utility area of the Session title row (the `创建/标准模式` line), left of the corner controls |
| Size | a fixed 380px × 28px slot, so the title row never reflows. On focus the field lifts out of flow as a 470px floating card (`position: absolute`) over the tab row, because the header must not grow |
| Blank conversations | the shipped header hides its whole title-row chrome while a conversation is still blank, so the same field also registers in `conversation.input.dock` (`order: -100`) and shows there until the title row appears. A module-level seat registry keeps exactly one copy on screen; the dock copy is the full-width, in-flow variant |
| Collapsed | one line; expands to four lines on focus; collapses on blur without losing text |
| Scope | text, chips, and the per-conversation switch are stored per conversation; a new conv

`conversation.send()` on the client is a pure pass-through — there is no
outgoing-prompt transform to hook. The durable, model-visible seam is the host's
`agent/pre-step`; when the claimed message batch contains a real user message
(a fresh send, not a tool-loop follow-up) this row appends one extra
`user/message`:

```
<session_requirement>
The user set a standing requirement for this whole conversation. Apply it to every reply until the user changes it.
<requirement>…</requirement>
<selected_skills>office-docx, office-xlsx</selected_skills>

It is committed through the harness's own `surfaceOp: "append"` path with
`source.kind = "session-requirement"`, so it lands in the transcript like the
built-in `/skill` invocation injection — it never impersonates a user gesture.

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/session-requirement?sessionId=…` | read one conversation's state (also reports `visible`) |
| `GET /api/session-requirement?mode=settings` | read the GUI switch alone, with no conversation |
| `POST /api/session-requirement` | write one conversation's state: `{ sessionId, requirementText, requirementEnabled, skillIds }` |
| `POST /api/session-requirement` `{ visible }` | flip the GUI switch alone |

State lives in `<DSH_HOME>/session-requirement.json`, written atomically
(`.tmp` + rename):

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1,
  "settings": { "visible": false },
  "sessions": {

Requests are rejected with `400` rather than silently corrected when `sessionId`
is malformed, the text exceeds `maxTextLength`, or `skillIds` is not a
deduplicated list of at most `maxSkills` skill names.

`/requirement` prints the current conversation's state; `/requirement clear`
clears and disables it.

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.x** (desktop or web), Cordis v4.
- No npm dependencies. The host half imports only Node built-ins; the browser
  half is a hand-written CJS bundle that takes `react` from the harness loader.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sunlei1214/dsh-session-requirement.git
```

Point your profile at the checkout:

```jsonc
// <DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>/package.json
"dependencies": { "dsh-session-requirement": "link:C:/path/to/dsh-session-requirement" },
"dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ …, "dsh-session-requirement" ] } }
```

Then reinstall the profile and restart DeepSeek Harness — the browser half ships
as a static client bundle, so a page refresh alone is not enough.

> **Use `link:`, not `file:`.** pnpm copies a `file:` directory dependency and
> caches it, so later edits never reach the profile. `link:` creates a junction
> (Windows) or symlink, so the profile always reads the current source.

Remove the dependency and the bundle entry, reinstall, restart. The host row
drops its route, its `agent/pre-step` listener, and flushes pending state on
dispose; the browser half removes its `<style data-plugin="dsh-session-requirement">`
node, its document listeners, its debounce timers, its caches, and aborts
in-flight requests. Deleting `<DSH_HOME>/session-requirement.json` is optional.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxSkills` | `10` | maximum chips per conversation |
| `maxTextLength` | `8000` | maximum requirement length |

```bash
node test/host-check.mjs
node test/client-check.mjs
```

(`npm test` runs both; if the PowerShell execution policy blocks `npm.ps1`, run
the two files directly.)

Two offline harnesses run against the real source files, with no harness install
required:

- `test/host-check.mjs` — a fake context, web server and skill registry. Covers
  both routes, the GUI switch (default off, flip, persist, and that a hidden row
  never attaches), every validation refusal, the atomic JSON sidecar, the
  pre-step injection (fresh send vs. tool-loop follow-up, disabled, empty,
  text-only, unknown and non-user-invocable skills, aborted signal), the
  `/requirement` command, and route removal on dispose.
- `test/client-check.mjs` — a minimal React hook runtime plus a fake DOM, driving
  the actual components: the GUI switch gating the row (absent while off,
  appearing live when flipped), collapsed/expanded rows, the grey toggle focusing
  instead of enabling, auto-enable on first content, manual off/on, chips, the
  `@` picker (filtering, arrows, `Enter`, `Esc`, click, empty state, load
  failure), dedupe, the cap, `Backspace`, per-conversation isolation, a late
  read not clobbering typed text, and a teardown that must leave no style node,
  listener, or pending write.

`test/verify-live.mjs` checks a **running** app after installing and restarting:

```bash
node test/verify-live.mjs           # read-only
node test/verify-live.mjs --write   # round-trip a write, then restore
```

It reports the state route, the GUI switch route, the boot manifest entry, and
the validation refusals. A `401` means the host half did not load — restart the
app.
